The impedance matching is achieved when the real part of \( Z_L \) is:

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a section of lossless transmission line with characteristic impedance Z0 = 50 Ω, and the right side is connected to load ZL. A section of transmission line near the load is labeled Z1 = 75 Ω, and the upper conductor from P to R is labeled with length 0.25λ, indicating a quarter-wavelength transformer section. There are also two parallel stubs in the figure: one connected between points P-Q, labeled Z1 = 75 Ω, S.C. stub, length 0.25λ, which is a short-circuit stub; the other connected between points R-S, labeled Z1 = 75 Ω, O.C. stub, length 0.5λ, which is an open-circuit stub. Reasoning: The input impedance of a short-circuited transmission-line stub is jZ0 tan(βl). When l = 0.25λ, βl = π/2, so the input impedance tends to infinity, equivalent to an open circuit. The input impedance of an open-circuited transmission-line stub is -jZ0 cot(βl). When l = 0.5λ, βl = π, so the input impedance also tends to infinity, equivalent to an open circuit. Therefore the two parallel stubs have no electrical effect on the main-line matching and can be ignored. What remains is a quarter-wavelength transformer with characteristic impedance Z1 = 75 Ω connecting the 50 Ω transmission line and the load ZL. The input impedance of the quarter-wavelength transformer is Zin = Z1^2 / ZL. The matching requirement is Zin = Z0 = 50 Ω, therefore 50 = 75^2 / ZL, giving ZL = 75^2 / 50 = 5625 / 50 = 112.5 Ω. Therefore, when matched, the real part of the load impedance is 112.5 Ω.

Therefore ignore both stubs electrically. The remaining network is a 75 Ω quarter-wave transformer between the 50 Ω line and ZL. Set the transformer input impedance equal to 50 Ω: 50 = 75^2 / ZL. Image description: On the left side of the figure is a section of lossless transmission line with characteristic impedance Z0 = 50 Ω, and the right side is connected to load ZL. A section of transmission line near the load is labeled Z1 = 75 Ω, and the upper conductor from P to R is labeled with length 0.25λ, indicating a quarter-wavelength transformer section. There are also two parallel stubs in the figure: one connected between points P-Q, labeled Z1 = 75 Ω, S.C. stub, length 0.25λ, which is a short-circuit stub; the other connected between points R-S, labeled Z1 = 75 Ω, O.C. stub, length 0.5λ, which is an open-circuit stub.
Reasoning: The input impedance of a short-circuited transmission-line stub is jZ0 tan(βl). When l = 0.25λ, βl = π/2, so the input impedance tends to infinity, equivalent to an open circuit. The input impedance of an open-circuited transmission-line stub is -jZ0 cot(βl). When l = 0.5λ, βl = π, so the input impedance also tends to infinity, equivalent to an open circuit. Therefore the two parallel stubs have no electrical effect on the main-line matching and can be ignored. What remains is a quarter-wavelength transformer with characteristic impedance Z1 = 75 Ω connecting the 50 Ω transmission line and the load ZL. The input impedance of the quarter-wavelength transformer is Zin = Z1^2 / ZL. The matching requirement is Zin = Z0 = 50 Ω, therefore 50 = 75^2 / ZL, giving ZL = 75^2 / 50 = 5625 / 50 = 112.5 Ω. Therefore, when matched, the real part of the load impedance is 112.5 Ω.
